correctness.rationale: The exact claim is rational coefficient HH for six combinatorial classes of eight-vertex Klein-bottle triangulations, not integral HH or arbitrary vertex counts. The Hochster bidegree convention (−k,2l), −k=p−l+1, maps p=0,l=2 to (−1,4) and p=1,l=4 to (−2,8), with the empty subset furnishing (0,0). Using all six facet lists, an independently written exact-Q chain computation re-enumerated 255 nonempty induced subcomplexes per class, checked every oriented boundary composition, verified no rational induced H2, computed degree-zero and first-homology restriction maps, checked all Hochster differential squares, and reproduced dimensions and ranks from the claim. All vertex links were cycles, f-vector (8,24,16), beta1(Q)=1. Incidence-graph isomorphism and all 36 legal directed 2-2 flips corroborate six distinct, flip-closed types; completeness among all possible eight-vertex Klein-bottle triangulations additionally uses the known Cervone classification rather than assuming orbit closure is a global census. No floating-point or modular surrogate was used for ranks.
risks: The proof relies on published completeness of the six eight-vertex types, whereas independent closure alone does not prove global completeness.
Rational HH only; no integral torsion classification.

value.rationale: This is a natural, complete, mathematically motivated six-object classification of a nonstandard moment-angle invariant for all vertex-minimal triangulations of one classical nonorientable surface. The exact HH profiles 2,4,6 differ despite identical homeomorphism type and f-vector, establishing that the invariant separates geometry/combinatorics invisible to these cruder invariants. Computing the induced cohomology deletion maps for all six types is not just a routine face-count deduction. The precise finite benchmark can be reused to test structural hypotheses and compare other nonorientable triangulations; no larger general theorem or integral calculation is claimed.
risks: Value is limited to exact rational finite classification; does not prove a parameterized family result.
